claims.text: The identity of X determines whether CrFeCoNiX forms a stable, coherent protective oxide above 900 °C.
CrFeCoNiSi forms a dense, adherent, low-growth-stress protective oxide above 900 °C.
CrFeCoNiAl forms a dense, adherent, low-growth-stress protective oxide above 900 °C.
The protective scales on the Si- and Al-containing alloys consist predominantly of SiO2 and Al2O3, respectively, possibly with Cr2O3 admixture.
CrFeCoNiMn forms relatively volatile, rapidly growing oxides above 900 °C.
Rapid growth of Mn-rich oxides produces porous scales that crack and spall.
The proposed comparison applies to single- or multiphase CrFeCoNiX solid solutions having homogeneous elemental distributions.
The controlled comparison exposes Si-, Mn-, and Al-containing alloys to the same oxidative or corrosive atmosphere above 900 °C while holding processing, grain size, and phase distribution similar.
Si and Al have high oxygen affinities.
Si- and Al-rich oxides are slow-growing and have low diffusivity.
Slow growth of Si- and Al-rich oxides minimizes internal stress and produces strong scale adhesion.
Volatility and rapid, uncontrolled growth of Mn oxides generate high internal stresses that cause cracking and spallation.
Compared with CrFeCoNiMn, CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiAl will have lower oxidation mass gains.
Compared with CrFeCoNiMn, CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiAl will form smoother, more adherent scales with less spallation.
CrFeCoNiMn is the baseline and is expected to promote unstable oxide formation.
The hypothesis is scoped to exposures at or above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres and to similarly processed single- or multiphase solid-solution alloys.
Differences in substrate grain size or phase constitution may modulate oxidation behavior.
Observation of a CrFeCoNiMn scale as continuous, coherent, low-mass-gain, and spallation-resistant as the Si- or Al-containing scales would falsify the hypothesis.
